title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.06500v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent's attention to task-relevant information. Existing token pruning and summarization methods remain constrained by discrete text representations, limiting the achievable compression ratios.   In this work, we challenge the prevailing assumption that agents must consume tool observations as explicit text tokens. To this end, we propose Coca-Cola, a continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents. Coca-Cola compresses tool observations into latent tokens and embeds them into the input embedding space of the agent. We further introduce Action-Preserving Training, which aligns the agent's next-action distributions under full and compressed observations. translated_title: 工具无需以文本形式发言：面向智能体的潜在上下文压缩
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体通常将原始工具输出直接附加到其上下文中。在多步交互过程中，冗长且嘈杂的观测内容会带来巨大的上下文开销，并稀释智能体对任务相关信息的注意力。现有的token剪枝和摘要方法仍受限于离散的文本表示，从而限制了可实现的压缩比率。在本工作中，我们挑战了“智能体必须以显式文本token的形式消费工具观测内容”这一普遍假设。为此，我们提出了Coca-Cola，一个面向大语言模型智能体的连续潜在上下文压缩模型。Coca-Cola将工具观测内容压缩为潜在token，并将其嵌入到智能体的输入嵌入空间中。我们进一步提出了动作保持训练，该方法在完整观测和压缩观测下对齐智能体的下一步动作分布。由此训练压缩模型学习到动作充分的潜在token，从而保留（原文在此处截断）……
tldr: 提出Coca-Cola连续潜在上下文压缩模型，将工具观测压缩为嵌入智能体输入空间的潜在token，并通过动作保持训练对齐动作分布，突破了离散文本表示的限制，实现更高的上下文压缩率。
en_tdlr: Proposes Coca-Cola, a continuous latent context compression model that compresses tool observations into latent tokens embedded in the agent's input space, with Action-Preserving Training aligning next-action distributions to surpass the limits of discrete text representations and achieve higher compression ratios.
